title.zh: 停不下来的西征：光绪元年的一笔账
title.en: The Expedition That Wouldn't Stop: A Ledger from the First Year of Guangxu

dek.zh: 海防要钱，西征也要钱。主张罢兵的人说停下来就是止损；左宗棠算的是另一笔账——有些开支，停下来一分也省不掉。
dek.en: Coastal defense needed money; so did the western expedition. Those who wanted to halt it called stopping a way to cut losses. Zuo Zongtang kept a different ledger — some costs, he argued, are not saved by stopping.

heading.en: The Opening: Two Claims on the Same Money

paras.zh: 光绪元年，领兵刚平定关陇的左宗棠正要出关，海防之议先起了。论者说，自高宗定新疆，「歲糜數百萬，此漏卮也」，如今「竭天下力贍西軍，無以待不虞」。帕夏是据有新疆南北诸城的塞外回酋（详见下节），论者主张照英国人的意思办：「許帕夏自立為國稱籓，罷西征，專力海防」。
paras.en: In the first year of the Guangxu reign, Zuo Zongtang, who had just led his forces to pacify Guanlong, was about to march out beyond the pass when the argument over coastal defense broke out first. Since the emperor Gaozong took Xinjiang, critics said, "several million a year have drained away, a leaky vessel"; now things had reached the point of "exhausting the strength of the whole realm to feed the western army, leaving nothing for the unforeseen." Pasha was the Muslim chief from beyond the frontier who held cities across southern and northern Xinjiang (more in the next section). The critics wanted to do as the British proposed: "let Pasha found his own state and pay homage as a vassal, call off the western expedition, concentrate on coastal defense."

heading.zh: 背景：帕夏、英俄与那块地
heading.en: The Background: Pasha, Britain, Russia, and the Ground Between

paras.zh: 要判断停不停，先看西边的开支在守什么。帕夏原出安集延部，传记写他「帕夏畏俄逼，闌入邊」，进边后先据喀什噶尔，蚕食南路诸城，又攻败占据乌鲁木齐的回妥明，遂并有北路伊犁诸城，收取赋入。他能役使回众，通使结援英、俄，购兵械自备；「英人陰助之，欲令別立為國，用捍蔽俄」——英国愿意他立国，好挡在俄国前面。
paras.en: Before judging whether to stop, look at what the western spending was protecting. Pasha came originally from the Andijan and, as the record puts it, "feared Russian pressure and slipped across the border." Inside it he first took Kashgar, nibbled away at the southern cities, and defeated Tuo Ming, the Muslim holding Ürümqi, so that he also possessed the Ili cities of the north and took their taxes. He commanded the Muslim population, kept envoys moving to draw in British and Russian support, and bought arms: "The English secretly helped him, wishing to set him up as a separate state, to serve as a buffer against Russia."

paras.zh: 北边，俄国也动了手。当时，俄以回数扰其边境，遽引兵逐回，取伊犁，且言将代取乌鲁木齐。
paras.en: In the north, Russia acted too. At that time, because the Muslims had repeatedly raided its border, Russia promptly sent troops to drive them out, took Ili, and said it would also take Ürümqi on China's behalf.

paras.zh: 一种解释是，此时摊开的已不是清廷与帕夏两方，而是清廷、帕夏、英、俄交错的局；所以“先停一停”要成立，得先说清停了以后这块地由谁看、谁来填。这是作者的推断。
paras.en: One reading of the position is that by now the table held not two parties but four — the court, Pasha, Britain and Russia, all entangled. For a pause to hold up, someone must first say who watches this ground during the pause, and who fills it. That is the author's inference.

heading.zh: 经过：从议罢西征到南北城尽复
heading.en: The Course: From Calling Off the Expedition to Recovering Both Halves

paras.zh: 海防一派的主张写得直白：西征是填不满的漏卮，一旦有不虞之事将无以应对，不如许帕夏自立为国、向中国称籓，把力量全数转去海防。传记说李鸿章于此「言之尤力」；本文所据的这一段只概述了论者的理由，没有单列他的论据。
paras.en: The coastal-defense case was stated flatly: the expedition was a vessel with a hole in it, and if anything unforeseen came, nothing would be left to meet it. Better to let Pasha set up a tributary state and turn every resource to the coast. The biography says Li Hongzhang pressed this hardest of all; the passage this piece relies on summarizes the critics' case and does not set out his own arguments.

paras.zh: 作者认为，左宗棠的反驳重心在账上，不过原话里也有「挫國威」这样的非财务理由。他认为割弃不等于省钱：关陇新平，不趁势收回旧地，反而让帕夏另立一国，是坐自遗患；帕夏若守不住，地不是归英就是入俄，地盘坐缩，边防要地尽失，防边的兵也减不掉。传记记其言：「關隴新平，不及時規還國家舊所沒地，而割棄使別為國，此坐自遺患。萬一帕夏不能有，不西為英並，即北折而入俄耳。吾地坐縮，邊要盡失，防邊兵不可減，糜餉自若。無益海防而挫國威，且長亂。此必不可。」作者以为，要害在中段：兵减不掉，饷照旧要花。
paras.en: One reading is that Zuo's answer rested chiefly on cost, though his words also cite damage to the state's prestige. Carving territory loose, he argued, did not save money: it stored up trouble, and if Pasha failed to hold the land it would fall to England or to Russia; the territory would shrink, every strategic point be lost, and the frontier troops could not be cut. The biography gives his words: "Guanlong has only just been pacified. Instead of recovering in good time the lands the state once lost, we carve them off and let another state be founded there — that is to store up trouble of our own making. Should Pasha fail to hold them, they will be swallowed by England in the west or fold north into Russia. Our territory shrinks of its own accord, every strategic point is lost, the frontier troops cannot be reduced, and the spending goes on as before. It does nothing for coastal defense, it damages our prestige, and it feeds disorder. This must not be." In the author's reading, the sting is in the middle: the troops cannot be cut, and the money flows out all the same.

paras.zh: 军机大臣文祥独赞同左宗棠之议，遂决策出塞，不罢兵，授左宗棠钦差大臣督军事，金顺副之。
paras.en: Wenxiang, a Grand Council minister, was the only one to favor Zuo's plan; the decision went to march beyond the pass rather than halt the campaign, with Zuo named Imperial Commissioner for military affairs and Jin Shun as his deputy.

paras.zh: 二年三月，大军次肃州。五月，锦棠（西征将领，与左宗棠并非一人；后来左宗棠奉诏入都时由他接替）北逾天山，会金顺军先攻乌鲁木齐，克之；原先窜处乌鲁木齐、仍隶帕夏的白彦虎遁走托克逊。九月，克玛纳斯南城，北路平，乃规南路。
paras.en: In the third month of the second year the army reached Suzhou. In the fifth, Jintang — a commander of the expedition and a different person from Zuo Zongtang; he would later replace Zuo when Zuo was summoned to the capital — crossed the Tianshan northward, joined Jin Shun's force, and took Ürümqi first; Bai Yanhu, who had been lodged in Ürümqi and still answered to Pasha, fled to Toksun. In the ninth month the southern city of Manas fell. The north was pacified; the plan turned south.

paras.zh: 军中有一道令，传记记作：「回部為安酋驅迫，厭亂久矣。大軍所至，勿淫掠，勿殘殺。王者之師如時雨，此其時也。」约束只有两条：不淫掠，不残杀。
paras.en: There was a general order in the army, which the biography records as: "The Muslims of the west were driven on by their Andijan chief and have long been sick of disorder. Wherever the great army goes, no rape or plunder, no slaughter. A kingly army is like a seasonable rain; this is the moment for it." Two prohibitions, and no more: no rape or plunder, and no killing.

paras.zh: 三年三月，锦棠攻克达坂城，悉释所擒缠回，纵之归。南路恟惧；次日收托克逊城，另部连破诸城隘，收吐鲁番，降缠回万余。接着是帕夏的结局：饮药死，其子伯克胡里戕其弟，走喀什噶尔。放回俘虏与南路恟惧，传记写在一处。
paras.en: In the third month of the third year Jintang took Dabancheng and released every Turkic Muslim he had captured, sending them home. Panic spread through the south; the next day Toksun fell, other columns stormed the cities and passes and recovered Turpan, and more than ten thousand Muslims submitted. Then Pasha's end: he drank poison and died; his son Bokhuli killed his own brother and fled to Kashgar. The freeing of the captives and the panic in the south are set down side by side.

paras.zh: 仗打到这一步，可以停了的声音第二次出现。库伦大臣上言，西事宜画定疆界；廷臣也说西征费钜，乌鲁木齐、吐鲁番既然到手，可以休兵。左宗棠叹道：「今時有可乘，乃為畫地縮守之策乎？」他抗疏争之，上以为然。
paras.en: The call to stop came a second time. The minister at Kulun reported that the western question should be settled by fixing a frontier, and courtiers argued the expedition cost too much: with Ürümqi and Turpan in hand, the army could rest. Zuo sighed: "The moment offers an opening — and we would settle for drawing lines on the map and shrinking back?" He sent up a forceful memorial against it; the throne agreed.

paras.zh: 还有一层分寸。时俄方与土耳其战，金顺请乘虚袭伊犁，左宗棠说：「不可。師不以正，彼有辭矣。」随后大军还定乌什，收南疆东四城，何步云以喀什汉城降；伯克胡里既纳白彦虎，乃效力攻汉城，大军至，复遁走俄；西四城相继下，左宗棠露布以闻，诏晋二等侯。
paras.en: There was also the matter of restraint. Russia was then at war with Turkey, and Jin Shun asked leave to strike Ili while it lay open. "No," said Zuo. "An army that does not act by right hands them their excuse." The army turned back to reduce Ushi, then took the four eastern cities of the south, and He Buyun surrendered the Chinese city of Kashgar. Bokhuli, having taken in Bai Yanhu, then threw his strength against that Chinese city; when the army arrived, he fled again into Russia. The four western cities fell in turn; Zuo announced the victory by public dispatch, and an edict raised him to second-class marquis.

paras.zh: 作者推断，这两句放在一起可以看出一条一致的标准：地要收回，但不能留下把柄。光绪元年讲的是割弃会挫国威、长乱，此处讲的是师不以正会让对方有辞。一种解释是，他衡量一个动作，不只看得地多少，还看事后守不守得住、辩不辩得清。这一归纳是作者的解释。
paras.en: The author's inference is that, set side by side, the two lines show one test: recover the ground, but leave no handle for the other side. In the first year of Guangxu the fear was that cession would damage prestige and feed disorder; here, that an army acting without right would hand Russia its excuse. One reading is that he judged a move by whether it could be held afterwards and defended in argument, not only by the land it gained. This generalization is the author's.

heading.zh: 分析：省钱的账要怎么算
heading.en: The Analysis: What the Ledger Has to Count

paras.zh: 南北既复，问题从打不打换成怎么守。四年正月，左宗棠条上新疆建行省事宜，并请与俄议还伊犁、交叛人二事。诏遣全权大臣崇厚使俄，俄以通商、分界、偿款三端相要，崇厚遽定约，为朝士所纠，议久不决。
paras.en: With north and south recovered, the question shifted from whether to fight to how to hold. In the first month of the fourth year Zuo laid out plans to make Xinjiang a regular province and asked that Russia be negotiated with over two things: the return of Ili and the handover of the rebels. A plenipotentiary envoy, Chong Hou, was sent to Russia. Russia pressed three demands — trade, boundaries, indemnity — and Chong Hou signed at once. Court officials impeached him, and the matter stayed open for a long time.

paras.zh: 左宗棠的奏折把这笔割地换和平的账摊开：俄视伊犁为外府，及我索地，俄则索偿卢布五百万元，所以俄还伊犁于俄无损，我所得不过一荒郊；崇厚又议畀俄陬尔果斯河及帖克斯河，是划伊犁西南之地归俄。他说：「茲一矢未加，遽捐要地」，界务不可许；俄商志在贸易，其政府广设领事，欲藉通商深入腹地，商务也不可许。他给的次序是：「當先之以議論，委婉而用機，次決之以戰陣，堅忍而求勝。」
paras.en: Zuo's memorial laid out the ledger for trading land for peace. Russia treated Ili as an outlying treasury, and when China asked for the land back, Russia demanded five million rubles in compensation; so returning Ili would cost Russia nothing, and what China got back would be "only a stretch of empty outskirts"; Chong Hou was meanwhile offering Russia the Korgos and Tekes rivers, ceding the southwest of Ili outright. "Not a single arrow has been loosed," Zuo wrote, "and we are to give up a key position at once": the boundary terms must not be granted. Russian merchants were after trade, but their government was planting consulates everywhere, hoping to use commerce to reach deep into the interior; those trade terms must not be granted either. His order of operations: "first let there be discussion, subtle and flexible; then decide it in battle, patient and determined to win."

paras.zh: 崇厚得罪去，命曾纪泽使俄更前约，左宗棠自请出屯哈密，规复伊犁。六年四月，他「輿櫬發肅州」——抬着棺材从肃州出发，五月抵哈密。俄闻王师大出，增兵守伊犁、纳林河，别以兵船翔海上，用震撼京师，天津、奉天、山东皆警。七月诏左宗棠入都备顾问，由西征将领锦棠接替他；传记称「俄亦懾我兵威」，明年正月和议成，交还伊犁，防海军皆罢。
paras.en: Chong Hou was disgraced and removed, and Zeng Jize sent to Russia to revise the treaty. Zuo asked to move out to Hami to prepare the recovery of Ili. In the fourth month of the sixth year he set out from Suzhou "carrying his coffin" and reached Hami in the fifth. Russia, hearing the imperial army was moving in force, reinforced Ili and the Naryn and put warships to sea to shake the capital; Tianjin, Fengtian and Shandong were all on alert. In the seventh month Zuo was summoned to the capital as an adviser, and Jintang, a commander of the expedition, replaced him; the biography says Russia too was cowed by the might of the Qing army. In the first month of the following year peace was concluded, Ili returned, and the coastal forces stood down.

paras.zh: 作者认为，这本账落到实处是后勤。史称其「用兵善審機，不常其方略」，筹西事尤以节兵裕饷为本谋；出塞凡二十月，新疆南北城尽复，传记归因于馈运饶给。另有屯田一节：初议西事他主兴屯田，闻者迂之；后来奏论关内外旧屯之弊，主张画兵农为二，简精壮为兵，散愿弱使屯垦，人服其老谋。
paras.en: One reading is that, in practice, the ledger came down to logistics. The biography says Zuo "was quick to judge the moment in war and never kept to one set of tactics," and that in western affairs he made economizing on troops and keeping pay and funds ample his first principle. Twenty months beyond the pass, and every city in north and south recovered: the biography credits the abundance of supply. There was garrison farming too. He argued for military colonies early on and was thought pedantic; then he set out the abuses of the old garrisons inside and outside the pass — men on the army rolls who could not also farm — and proposed dividing the two, keeping the strong as soldiers, settling the meek and the weak on the land. Then people respected the long view behind it.

paras.zh: 仗打赢之后，外部的看法也变了。国家承平久，武备弛不振，而海外诸国争言富强，虽中国屡平大难，仍私议以为脆弱；及左宗棠平帕夏，外国乃稍稍传说之。京师民间另有一则传言：左宗棠初入京师时，内城有教堂高楼俯瞰宫殿，民间讙言「左侯至，樓即毀矣」；后出示谕晓，传言乃止。传记以「其威望在人如此」收束此事，随即转笔：左宗棠在军机、译署任上（此职系入觐后所授，传记记于前文），「同列頗厭苦之」，他本人也「自不樂居內，引疾乞退」。
paras.en: After the victories, opinion abroad shifted. The empire had been at peace so long that its armaments had gone slack, while the overseas powers vied with one another in talk of wealth and power; even though China had put down one great crisis after another, they still privately judged it frail. Once Zuo had dealt with Pasha, the foreigners began to spread the word about him. Within the capital there was a separate, domestic rumor: when Zuo first entered the capital, a church tower in the Inner City overlooked the palace, and people in the city said the tower would come down once the Marquis Zuo arrived; a notice was posted to explain, and the talk stopped. The biography closes the episode by calling it a measure of his prestige, then turns: in his posts at the Grand Council and the foreign-affairs office (conferred after his audience, as the biography records earlier), his colleagues found him a great trial, and Zuo himself, unhappy serving in the capital, pleaded illness and asked to retire.

paras.zh: 作者推断，把光绪元年那场争论拆开，可以得到三个可复用的判断依据：停下来之后要守的东西还守不守得住；省下的开支是不是真省下来；推迟的代价会不会转嫁给后面的人。一种解释是，左宗棠的反对之所以立得住，不在于西征更值钱，而在于割弃并不改变成本结构——地缩了，兵不减，饷照旧，另外还多出后患。三个判断依据是作者的归纳；成本结构一点的核心，即「防邊兵不可減，糜餉自若」，出自传记所记左宗棠原话。
paras.en: The author's reading is that unpacking that first-year argument yields three reusable tests: can what you were protecting still be held once you stop? Is the money you save actually saved? Does the cost of delay simply pass to whoever comes next? One reading is that Zuo's objection held not because the expedition was worth more, but because cession left the cost structure untouched — less territory, the same troops, the same spending, and trouble added. The three tests are the author's summary; the core of the cost-structure point — the frontier troops cannot be reduced and the spending goes on as before — comes from Zuo's own words as the biography records them.

heading.en: Today: Is a Pause the Same as Cutting Losses?

paras.zh: 今天类似的场面往往披着预算外衣。比如一家软件公司，跑了十年的老系统每年吃掉大半运维预算，有人提议冻结投入、把人力全挪去做新平台。照光绪元年那本账，先问三句：停了以后，老客户的合同义务、历史数据、监管留存由谁守？冻结投入省下的是真金白银，还是把改造成本推到系统崩掉那天，外加违约和迁移的双份账？推迟的代价由谁背——这届管理层的报表，还是三年后接手的人？
paras.en: Scenes like this usually turn up in budget clothing. A software company has run a ten-year-old system that eats most of the operations budget each year, and someone proposes freezing investment and moving everyone to a new platform. By the ledger of the first year of Guangxu, three questions come first. Once you stop, who keeps the obligations to existing customers, the historical data, the records the regulator requires? Does the frozen spending really come back as cash, or does it push the cost of rebuilding to the day the system fails, with breach and migration billed on top? And who carries the delay — this management's numbers, or whoever inherits it in three years?

paras.zh: 再如一座城市的财政：一条年年亏损的郊区公交线被称为漏卮，有人主张砍掉，把补贴挪给新修的地铁延伸线。砍之前同样要问：沿线通勤、就医的人由谁接走？省下的补贴会不会被新线初期的亏损吃掉？几年后若不得不重开，重开的成本是否比维持更高？三问都有答案，才谈得上取舍。
paras.en: Or a city's finances. A suburban bus route that loses money every year is called a leaky vessel; someone wants to cut it and move the subsidy to a new metro extension. Before cutting: who picks up the commuters and the patients along the route? Will the new line's own early losses swallow the subsidy saved? And if the route must be revived in a few years, will reopening cost more than keeping it going? Only when all three have answers is there a trade-off to speak of.

heading.en: The Limits: Where This Material Comes From

paras.zh: 本文全部史实出自《清史稿·左宗棠传》一处传记，成书刊行远在事件之后，是单一史源。本文未查阅同时期奏疏原文、上谕原件，也未查阅李鸿章、帕夏、俄方、崇厚一方的记载以作对勘；传中所引奏疏、诏书为史家转引，未必是全文。文中的宗棠曰、歎曰，以及那道令曰，都是史家记述，未必是逐字原话；英文版中的引语均为作者自文言译出。本文所据段落中，文祥独善宗棠议、李鸿章言之尤力各只有一句，本文没有替任何一方补写论据或心理动机。
paras.en: Every fact here comes from a single source: the biography of Zuo Zongtang in the Draft History of the Qing, compiled and printed long after the events it describes. This piece did not consult original memorials, edict originals, or accounts by Li Hongzhang, Pasha, the Russian side or Chong Hou to check against it; the memorial and edict wording quoted in the biography comes to us through the compilers and is not necessarily complete. The "Zuo said," "Zuo sighed," and the general order are the historian's rendering and need not be verbatim. All quotations in the English text are the author's translations from the classical Chinese. In the passages this piece relies on, Wenxiang's support and Li Hongzhang's advocacy each appear in a single sentence, and this piece writes in no arguments or motives for either.

paras.zh: 数字一律照录原文，本文未核验其口径与范围（例如岁糜数百万是常年军费还是协饷缺口，降缠回万余亦同）。原文纪年用光绪元年、二年、三年、四年、六年，本文不换算公元；明年正月和议成的明年，指前文所记年份的下一年。另需点明：帕夏畏俄逼是原文的表述，本文转述时已注明出自传记。至于下一节的替代选择与两段现代场景，都是作者为说明判断方法所加。
paras.en: Numbers are reproduced as written, and this piece has not verified their basis or scope (for instance, whether "several million a year" means standing military spending or a shortfall in provincial remittances; the same goes for the "more than ten thousand" who submitted). Dates stay in the original — the first, second, third, fourth and sixth years of Guangxu — and are not converted; "the first month of the following year" means the year after the one just named. One more point: "Pasha feared Russian pressure" is the source's own phrasing, flagged here as the biography's. The alternative option below and the two modern scenes are the author's additions, made to show a method of judgment.

scenario.zh: 一家开了二十年的小工厂，旧设备改造的投入被股东称作漏卮，同时刚好接到一笔新订单，需要先买新设备；钱只够先顾一头，砍掉旧投入看起来最像止损。
scenario.en: A small factory that has been running for twenty years: shareholders call the spending on upgrading its old equipment a leaky vessel, and just then a new order arrives that needs new equipment bought first. The money covers only one of the two, and cutting the old investment looks exactly like cutting losses.

question.zh: 资源只能先给一头时，我凭什么说这是取舍，而不是逃避？
question.en: When resources can only go to one of the two, on what grounds do I call this a trade-off rather than evasion?

assumptions.zh: 假设旧设备若完全停改，短期内现金确实宽裕，但旧线良率下降，返工与停机风险上升；新订单有交付期限，回款在交付之后。
assumptions.en: Assume that if the upgrade is stopped entirely, cash does loosen in the short term; but yield on the old line falls, and rework and downtime risks rise. The new order has a delivery deadline, and payment arrives only after delivery.

steps.zh: 先把三条依据各写一行：停下来之后要守的东西（老订单的交付、既有客户的合同）还守不守得住；省下的开支是否真省下来，还是把改造成本、违约金和日后重启的费用推到后面；推迟的代价由谁承担，会不会转嫁给下一任厂长或下一批工人。再把两条路各写成一行账：不停，钱花在哪里、换回什么；停，省下什么、欠下什么。两行账都写得出，才算算过。
steps.en: Write the three tests out, one line each. First, what has to be protected once you stop — delivery on the old orders, existing customer contracts — and can it still be protected? Second, is the spending genuinely saved, or are the upgrade cost, penalties and the eventual cost of restarting simply pushed downstream? Third, who absorbs the cost of delay, and does it fall on the next plant manager or the next crew? Then write each path as a single line of accounts: not stopping — where the money goes, what it buys; stopping — what is saved, what is owed. Both lines written out, and only then has the sum been done.

alternative.zh: 作者提出的替代选择：既不停全款、也不全停，而是把旧线改造拆成最小的一步，先改最影响良率的一环，同时按新订单的回款节奏排设备采购的先后；或者反过来，先保新订单，把旧线维持在最低安全水平，并写明一个复核时点，到时用同一组问题再算一遍。这些方案是作者为说明判断方法所加。
alternative.en: The alternative the author suggests: neither full funding nor a full stop, but break the old-line upgrade into its smallest first step, fix the single stage that most affects yield, and stage the equipment purchases against the new order's payment schedule. Or the reverse: protect the new order first, hold the old line at a minimum safe level, and set a review date at which the same questions are run again. These options are the author's addition to show the method.

uncertainty_note.zh: 全文仅据《清史稿·左宗棠传》单一史源，成书远晚于事件；本文未查阅同期奏疏、上谕原件或对方记载以作对勘，传中所引奏、诏为史家转引，未必是全文；引语为史家记述，未必逐字，英文版引语为作者译文；数字照录，本文未核验其口径；纪年不换算公元；「帕夏畏俄逼」为原文表述；替代选择与现代场景均为作者所加。
uncertainty_note.en: Everything rests on a single source, the biography of Zuo Zongtang in the Draft History of the Qing, compiled long after the events; this piece did not consult original memorials, edicts or opposing accounts to check against it, and the memorials and edicts quoted in the biography come through the compilers and are not necessarily complete. Quotations are the historian's rendering and may not be verbatim, and English quotations are the author's translations; numbers are reproduced as written, and their scope has not been verified here; dates are not converted out of the Guangxu reign years; "Pasha feared Russian pressure" is the source's own phrasing; and the modern scenes and the alternative option are the author's additions.

preheader.zh: 两笔钱都该花、只能先花一笔的时候，「先停一停」到底省了什么
preheader.en: When two needs both look urgent and you can only fund one, what does pausing the other actually save?
